flagship_use_case: AI Application Processing Agent — business submits an application with Arabic/English documents; Submission → Document Agent → OCR → Extraction → Knowledge Agent → Qdrant + Neo4j → Rules → Planner → Verification → Human Approval → Nazo/MOET Mock API → Completion

frozen_constraints.graphrag: CLOSED — resolver 0.82, depth 1, graph_top_k 8, hop_decay 0.55, fusion 0.60, max_nodes 100. Do not change, do not re-tune.
frozen_constraints.embeddings: Do NOT route through the Model Gateway — it hosts no embedding model; the frozen 174-case baseline and the 993-point corporate_memory collection were produced by bge-small-en-v1.5 at 384 dims.
frozen_constraints.messaging: No Redis. No NATS. In-process bus behind MessageBus/WorkQueue Protocols; EventEnvelope with non-optional tenant_id.

items.capability: RETRIEVE — GraphRAG exposed to the authoritative runtime
items.objective: Register the frozen GraphRAG pipeline as a typed Tool on the LangGraph runtime so the demo's retrieval step returns Qdrant chunks AND graph entities with citations.

items.new_work: One handler + one Tool registration ('knowledge_search') rendering RankedContextBundle as cited excerpts. Pass NO retrieval parameters — the six frozen values are already the defaults (providers/graph.py:35 top_k=8; depth -> GRAPH_RETRIEVAL_DEPTH=1). Do not modify search_documents; this is additive.
items.acceptance_test: /agent/chat answers a corpus question with citations from both Qdrant and Neo4j; a test asserts the six frozen parameters are unchanged at the call site; the user-scoped ACL from registry.py:143 is preserved; backend/evals/ re-runs within its unchanged score band.
items.demo_value: Without this the authoritative runtime has no graph retrieval at all — search_documents is Qdrant-only. This is the RETRIEVE stage.
items.production_followup: Tenant-scoped graph reads with a golden-set equivalence test before any org filter is enabled on a production read path.
items.notes: FIRST IMPLEMENTATION TASK. Purely additive, near-zero regression risk, unblocks the Knowledge Agent, Verification Agent, rules step and citation panel.

Canonical names: subject_id / user_uuid / tenant_id / tenant_key. The bare name user_id is forbidden on the contract.
items.acceptance_test: Two-tenant fixture: Tenant A cannot read Tenant B's Postgres rows, Qdrant points or uploaded documents. Each case has a second variant authenticated via X-Internal-Token with a forged X-Internal-User.
items.demo_value: The stated P0-2 acceptance criterion, and the difference between a demo and a platform.
items.production_followup: All 11 propagation surfaces; NOT NULL backfill; app-Postgres RLS; CI Gate 8 enforcing.

items.objective: Give submitted application documents an intake path that is tenant-scoped from the first byte, reusing the existing extraction and OCR primitives.

items.objective: Ensure every model call on the POC path flows through the Model Gateway, and redirect the known direct Azure OpenAI bypass.

items.demo_value: 'All model calls flow through the Model Gateway' is a claim the demo must be able to survive being asked about.
items.production_followup: Port plan()/fallback/cost telemetry onto llm.py; ModelProfile per tenant; delete the Azure branch; CI Gate 3 enforcing.
items.notes: Verified: this is an ALIAS SWAP, not an integration — a read-only probe of GET :4000/model/info shows gpt-4.1 already registered as azure/gpt-4.1. DASHBOARD_LLM=azure is live in .env:55 and is reachable from the shipped /agent/chat surface via unified.py:169,172.

items.capability: Tool Gateway — the Agent -> Tool Gateway -> Connector boundary
items.objective: Make the typed Tool registry the single dispatch point for every tool call on the POC path, with a declared boundary to connectors.

items.new_work: Formalise dispatch through one gateway function; add Tool v1 fields 'pack' and 'group'; collapse outbound-ness to ONE source of truth before any policy consumes it.

Collapse BEFORE PolicyInterface, or the wrong answer is encoded into the new abstraction.

items.objective: One decision point answering tool authorization, tenant authorization, high-risk classification and human-approval requirement, enforcing on the POC path.

items.new_work: A three-way exhaustive Effect (allow/deny/approval_required) plus a composite engine taking the MOST RESTRICTIVE answer across the existing mechanisms; PolicyRequest embeds TenantContext; every decision emits a policy.decision.evaluated event.
items.acceptance_test: A denied tool call is refused at the executor; a high-risk action returns approval_required and does NOT execute; the web_search divergence (approval-gated at skills.py:409 vs auto-executed via guardrails) resolves to the restrictive answer without editing either source.
items.demo_value: DECIDE. Also the mechanism that makes Scenario 3 real rather than scripted.
items.production_followup: Full OPA/Rego, externalised per tenant; shadow-mode divergence ratchet across the whole surface, not just the POC path.
items.notes: Phase 0 specified SHADOW mode platform-wide. The POC needs a REAL decision on the demo path — so: enforcing on the POC path, shadow everywhere else. State the enforced surface explicitly (RISK R-10).

A sixth client at api/client.ts:71 posts to a bare /chat.

items.objective: Produce a bounded, inspectable plan: task decomposition, agent selection, tool selection, model selection, dependency ordering, approval detection, retry/failure handling.

items.production_followup: Replanning, learned routing, cost-aware model selection, per-run budgets.
items.notes: RISK R-8. 'No uncontrolled autonomous loop' is a hard constraint: the plan is data, the caps are enforced by test, and the planner never bypasses the policy point.

items.objective: Define the Agent interface and the EventEnvelope that agents exchange, so collaboration is a contract rather than a call graph.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: The delegate tool (agents.py:67-96) — already runs a specialist as a nested graph.run_turn with its own persona and allowlist; backend/events.py as the audit sink; x-trace-id already stamped at main.py:906

items.acceptance_test: Every inter-agent message is an EventEnvelope with a non-null tenant_id; event_type matches the three-token grammar; no producer composes a transport address itself; the envelope round-trips through the events table.
items.demo_value: COLLABORATE, and the data behind the agent timeline in the explainability panel.
items.production_followup: Promote envelope fields to real columns; per-consumer-group cursors; broker adapter.
items.notes: An Optional tenant_id means every consumer writes 'if e.tenant_id' forever. trace_id and tenant_id both already exist in-process and merely need carrying.

items.objective: An agent that takes a submission, runs extraction/OCR, and produces typed fields with provenance back to the source span.

items.new_work: Agent definition (persona, allowlist, model) + orchestration of intake -> extract -> structured fields.
items.acceptance_test: A submitted PDF yields typed fields, each carrying the OCR span it came from; a scanned/photographed PDF routes through the VLM path; the agent never calls an outbound tool.
items.demo_value: SEE. 'What did it understand?' in the explainability panel.
items.production_followup: Page-level jobs, dedicated OCR worker, confidence scores, human correction loop.
items.notes: FINDING F-1: OCR already exists, is VLM-based at temperature=0 and 150 dpi, is multilingual by construction, and already flows through the Model Gateway. Its docstring cites a photographed business licence — the exact flagship shape.

items.objective: An agent that answers requirement and precedent questions from the corpus, returning citations from both Qdrant and Neo4j.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: POC-1's knowledge_search tool over the frozen GraphRAG pipeline; the 993-point corporate_memory collection; the 522-entity / 3414-relationship graph
items.new_work: Agent definition + citation rendering.

items.demo_value: RETRIEVE. 'Which documents were retrieved?' — and the grounding that makes Scenario 1 credible.
items.production_followup: Tenant-scoped graph reads; freshness; retrieval quality evaluation as a suite.
items.notes: GraphRAG is CLOSED. This agent consumes it; it must not tune it.

items.objective: An agent that checks the decision and the extracted fields against retrieved evidence, and blocks completion on conflict.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: The dashboard's evidence-verification ledger pattern (backend/dashboard/) as the reference; GraphRAG citations
items.new_work: Agent definition + field-by-field conflict detection with both sources cited.
items.acceptance_test: Scenario 2: the agent detects a legal-entity-name conflict between the trade licence and the application form, cites both with page/chunk provenance, and blocks completion; it does not 'resolve' the conflict by choosing one.
items.demo_value: VERIFY. The scenario that most convinces a sceptical reviewer — the system says 'I don't know, and here is exactly why.'
items.production_followup: Generalise to a global critic; confidence calibration; conflict taxonomy.
items.notes: Verification must be a DISTINCT agent, not a prompt instruction on the planner — otherwise the demo cannot show it as a separate step.

items.objective: Turn verbatim OCR text into typed application fields with provenance, because OCR alone gives prose, not decisions.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: _ocr_pdf_via_vision output; the Model Gateway; LLM_VISION_MODEL
items.new_work: A field schema for the application type plus an extraction step that records, per field, the source span it came from.
items.acceptance_test: Every extracted field carries a source span; a missing field is reported as absent rather than guessed; extraction is deterministic at temperature=0 across three consecutive runs on the same document.
items.demo_value: 'What did it understand?' — the panel that opens the demo.
items.production_followup: Confidence scores; human correction loop; per-document-type schemas as pack content.

items.objective: A small declarative rule set that fires visibly, deterministically, and with citations.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: PolicyInterface from POC-6 as the enforcement seam; GraphRAG citations as the evidence source
items.new_work: A versioned rule set (id, version, inputs, predicate, outcome) covering document completeness, consistency and risk threshold. Rules are DETERMINISTIC CODE, never model judgement.
items.acceptance_test: Scenario 1 fires the missing-document rule by id; Scenario 3 fires the risk-threshold rule; each firing records rule id, version, inputs and outcome; the same inputs produce the same firings across runs.
items.demo_value: 'Which rules fired?' — and the determinism that makes the demo repeatable.
items.production_followup: Rules service, authoring UI, per-tenant rule packs, rule evaluation history.
items.notes: RISK R-12 mitigation: keeping rules as code rather than model judgement is what makes three scripted scenarios survive LLM nondeterminism.

items.capability: RETRIEVE — close the ingestion loop into Neo4j
items.objective: Make a newly submitted document visible to the graph, not only to Qdrant.

items.new_work: Wire entity extraction for submitted documents into the graph write path, with org as an ADDITIVE property.

CONSTRAINT: queries.py:193 MERGEs on (:Entity {id}) ALONE — org scoping must be an additive property plus a query-time filter, never a change to that identity key, or every expected_graph_nodes value in all 174 cases is invalidated.

items.objective: One durable record per decision linking tenant, user, plan, retrieved evidence, rules fired, policy decision, approver and action result.

items.production_followup: Retention, partitioning, rollups; admin-isolated audit surface.
items.notes: Use repo.log_event's signature as the shape of record — it is the only writer that can express run_id and an explicit tenant. Do NOT let the demo write through the SQLite events branch, which has no org column at all.

items.objective: One trace spanning user -> planner -> agent -> model -> retrieval -> tool -> approval -> result.

items.objective: A single UI surface answering the eight questions the brief requires the system to visibly explain.

items.new_work: A panel rendering: understood / planned / agents run / documents retrieved / rules fired / why approval / action taken / full trace.

items.demo_value: The most convincing scenario for a sceptical reviewer: the system says 'I don't know, and here is exactly why.'
items.production_followup: Conflict taxonomy; confidence calibration; resolution workflow.

items.objective: Demonstrate that the approval gate is real, enforced at the executor, and exactly-once.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: The persisted approval store with compare-and-swap decide(); graph.resume(); the Approvals UI
items.new_work: Fixture application above the risk threshold with complete, consistent documents, plus the scripted walkthrough.
items.acceptance_test: The outbound call does NOT happen before approval; the human sees the full explanation; approving executes exactly once; a replayed approval is refused; the audit record links decision -> policy -> approver -> action -> result.

items.production_followup: Approval expiry, assignment, delegation, bulk decisions.

items.objective: Define every contract as a type so Phases 5-8 inherit one boundary, while implementing only what the POC path traverses.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: Nothing — the package does not exist. backend/ is a namespace package (no backend/__init__.py), so a dependency-free contracts package is achievable.

items.objective: Support agent collaboration with the simplest safe mechanism while preserving a migration path to NATS JetStream.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: The single-uvicorn-process deployment (no --workers) — in-process fan-out is already a dict of asyncio queues; storage/indexing.py as the durable-state-machine reference
items.new_work: backend/messaging/ with MessageBus and WorkQueue Protocols and an in-process adapter preserving today's behaviour exactly. ADR-0001 recording the Postgres-queue architectural recommendation and trigger thresholds T1-T6.
items.acceptance_test: No module outside the adapter package imports a transport client, enforced by a CI rule; swapping the adapter changes no agent code; no Redis or NATS dependency is added.
items.demo_value: Lets the POC claim a migration path without paying for a broker, and makes the boundary visibly replaceable.
items.production_followup: Postgres jobs table + outbox drain (option D); JetStream when T1 and T4 fire together.
items.notes: Decision spike complete: architecturally (D) Postgres; implementationally build no transport. The host Redis is DISQUALIFIED for durable work — shared with another application's live Celery broker, no requirepass, allkeys-lru eviction.

items.objective: Make the three scenarios repeatable from a clean state, in front of an audience.
items.existing_component_to_reuse: backend/evals/ fixture patterns; the existing tenant/org provisioning path
items.new_work: Two demo tenants; fixture document sets for all three scenarios; a reset script; pinned AGANETI_DATA_BACKEND=postgres; temperature=0 on all decision paths.
items.acceptance_test: Three consecutive full runs from reset produce the same rule firings, the same policy decisions and the same approval requirements. Answer prose may vary; DECISIONS may not.
items.demo_value: The difference between a demo that works and a demo that worked once.
items.production_followup: Seed/teardown as a pack contract.
items.notes: RISK R-12: LLM nondeterminism was MEASURED at 62/174 differing answers between identical runs, and found to be session-state dependent. Determinism must come from rules-as-code and policy-as-code, not from hoping the model repeats itself. RISK R-6: AGANETI_DATA_BACKEND defaults to sqlite, which would silently give the demo a different system of record than production.
